competency_fulfillment.rationale: Seeds 42-46 all ask 'A shape is divided into 8 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. What fraction of the shape is shaded?', which exercises the verb 'identify' but never 'represent' - the pupil selects a printed symbol rather than partitioning or shading a region. The key 1/8 is itself correct.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The wording explicitly names denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8, yet every one of the five seeds (42, 43, 44, 45, 46) fixes the denominator at 8. Halves, thirds, fourths, fifths and sixths are never generated, so five of the six named sub-cases are missing.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sentence length and the vocabulary 'equal parts' and 'shaded' suit Grade 2 Quarter 4, but the distractor '8/1' puts an improper fraction greater than one in front of pupils who have only met unit fractions less than one, inviting a misconception this node cannot resolve.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All five seeds emit a byte-identical stem; only the A-D option order rotates (the key 1/8 sits at C, A, D, C, then B). There is no area-model versus set-model versus number-line variation and no shaded-versus-unshaded rephrasing anywhere in the sample.

competency_alignment.rationale: Because seeds 42 through 46 are the same item with the same answer, there is no progression from an easy denominator such as halves toward eighths. Difficulty is perfectly flat, so repeated practice cannot build unit-fraction understanding across the named denominator set.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The distractor '3/16' uses denominator 16, outside this competency's explicit ceiling set of {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8}, exposing Grade 2 pupils to sixteenths the node never teaches; it is also not a unit fraction.
